claim: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic and relapsing immune-mediated disorder characterized by intestinal inflammation and epithelial injury.
source: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic and relapsing immune-mediated disorder characterized by intestinal inflammation and epithelial injury.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about IBD that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: CTLA-4 has been implicated as a genetic factor in IBD through genome-wide association studies.
source: The underlying causes of IBD are not fully understood, but genetic factors have been implicated in genome-wide association studies, including CTLA-4, an essential negative regulator of T cell activation.
evidence: This claim references genome-wide association studies that have identified CTLA-4 as a genetic factor in IBD.

claim: Establishing a direct link between CTLA-4 and IBD has been challenging due to the early lethality of CTLA-4 knockout mice.
source: However, establishing a direct link between CTLA-4 and IBD has been challenging due to the early lethality of CTLA-4 knockout mice.
evidence: This claim is based on known limitations of CTLA-4 knockout mouse models from prior research.

claim: Zebrafish Ctla-4 homolog was identified in this study.
source: In this study, we identified zebrafish Ctla-4 homolog and investigated its role in maintaining intestinal immune homeostasis by generating a Ctla-4-deficient (ctla-4-/-) zebrafish line.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study describing the identification of the zebrafish Ctla-4 homolog.

claim: Ctla-4-deficient zebrafish exhibited reduced weight.
source: These mutant zebrafish exhibited reduced weight, along with impaired epithelial barrier integrity and lymphocytic infiltration in their intestines.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations of the ctla-4-/- zebrafish phenotype.

claim: Ctla-4-deficient zebrafish exhibited impaired epithelial barrier integrity.
source: These mutant zebrafish exhibited reduced weight, along with impaired epithelial barrier integrity and lymphocytic infiltration in their intestines.
evidence: This claim is supported by histological and ultrastructural analysis of the intestines.

claim: Ctla-4-deficient zebrafish exhibited lymphocytic infiltration in their intestines.
source: These mutant zebrafish exhibited reduced weight, along with impaired epithelial barrier integrity and lymphocytic infiltration in their intestines.
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis showing inflammatory cell infiltration.

claim: Transcriptomics analysis revealed upregulation of inflammation-related genes in ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: Transcriptomics analysis revealed upregulation of inflammation-related genes, disturbing immune system homeostasis.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-sequencing data comparing wild-type and ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis indicated increased Th2 cells in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines.
source: Moreover, single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis indicated increased Th2 cells and interleukin 13 expression, along with decreased innate lymphoid cells and upregulated proinflammatory cytokines.
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell RNA-sequencing data showing changes in cell populations.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis indicated increased interleukin 13 expression in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines.
source: Moreover, single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis indicated increased Th2 cells and interleukin 13 expression, along with decreased innate lymphoid cells and upregulated proinflammatory cytokines.
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell RNA-sequencing data showing gene expression changes.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis indicated decreased innate lymphoid cells in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines.
source: Moreover, single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis indicated increased Th2 cells and interleukin 13 expression, along with decreased innate lymphoid cells and upregulated proinflammatory cytokines.
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell RNA-sequencing data showing changes in cell populations.

claim: Ctla-4-deficient zebrafish exhibited reduced diversity of intestinal microbiota.
source: Additionally, Ctla-4-deficient zebrafish exhibited reduced diversity and an altered composition of the intestinal microbiota.
evidence: This claim is supported by 16S rRNA gene sequencing analysis of intestinal microbiota.

claim: Ctla-4-deficient zebrafish exhibited altered composition of the intestinal microbiota.
source: Additionally, Ctla-4-deficient zebrafish exhibited reduced diversity and an altered composition of the intestinal microbiota.
evidence: This claim is supported by 16S rRNA gene sequencing analysis of intestinal microbiota.

claim: The phenotypes in ctla-4-/- zebrafish closely resemble those found in mammalian IBD.
source: All these phenotypes closely resemble those found in mammalian IBD.
evidence: This is a comparative inference based on the observed phenotypes and known characteristics of mammalian IBD.

claim: Supplementation with Ctla-4-Ig successfully alleviated intestinal inflammation in ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: Lastly, supplementation with Ctla-4-Ig successfully alleviated intestinal inflammation in these mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from in vivo administration assays showing reduced inflammation.

claim: Ctla-4 plays a pivotal role in maintaining intestinal homeostasis.
source: Altogether, our findings demonstrate the pivotal role of Ctla-4 in maintaining intestinal homeostasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the collective experimental findings in the study.

claim: The study offers substantial evidence linking CTLA-4 to IBD.
source: Additionally, they offer substantial evidence linking CTLA-4 to IBD and establish a novel zebrafish model for investigating both the pathogenesis and potential treatments.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the totality of experimental findings in the study.

claim: The study establishes a novel zebrafish model for investigating IBD pathogenesis and potential treatments.
source: Additionally, they offer substantial evidence linking CTLA-4 to IBD and establish a novel zebrafish model for investigating both the pathogenesis and potential treatments.
evidence: This is a summary claim about the contribution of the study.

claim: IBD includes Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.
source: IBD, including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, refers to a group of chronic relapsing inflammation disorders affecting the gastrointestinal tract, that have been increasing in prevalence worldwide (Hodson, 2016).
evidence: This is a definitional statement supported by a citation.

claim: IBD has been increasing in prevalence worldwide.
source: IBD, including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, refers to a group of chronic relapsing inflammation disorders affecting the gastrointestinal tract, that have been increasing in prevalence worldwide (Hodson, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hodson, 2016.

claim: The precise etiology of IBD has yet to be fully elucidated.
source: The precise etiology of IBD has yet to be fully elucidated.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: IBD tends to run in families and is linked to genetic factors.
source: Conventional epidemiological studies have indicated that IBD tends to run in families and is linked to genetic factors (Zhang and Li, 2014; Uniken Venema et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to epidemiological studies.

claim: Susceptibility gene patterns for IBD differ significantly among various geographic populations.
source: However, research also suggested that susceptibility gene patterns differ significantly among various geographic populations.
evidence: This claim is based on research findings about genetic variation in IBD susceptibility.

claim: IBD involves a complicated interaction involving host genetics, disrupted intestinal microbiota, environmental triggers, and abnormal immune responses.
source: Current evidence points towards a complicated interaction involving host genetics, disrupted intestinal microbiota, environmental triggers, and abnormal immune responses (Loftus, 2004; Khor et al., 2011; Neurath, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations describing the multifactorial nature of IBD.

claim: Genetically susceptible individuals with IBD exhibit defects in intracellular pattern-recognition receptors such as TLR and NLRs.
source: Research on humans with Crohn's disease and mouse models of IBD has shown that genetically susceptible individuals exhibit defects in intracellular pattern-recognition receptors (PRRs), such as toll-like receptors (TLR) and nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptors (NLRs), which are responsible for initiating innate immune responses to eliminate harmful bacteria (Kordjazy et al., 2018; Horowitz et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research on humans and mouse models.

claim: Genetic variations in TNFSF15 and IL23R genes have been associated with an increased risk of developing Crohn's disease.
source: Genetic variations in the tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 15 (TNFSF15) and interleukin 23 receptor (IL23R) genes, both involved in suppressing inflammation, have been associated with an increased risk of developing Crohn's disease (Duerr et al., 2006; Tremelling et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to genetic association studies.

claim: CTLA-4 is one of the most well-established immune checkpoint molecules expressed predominantly on T cells.
source: Cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen-4 (CTLA-4), also known as CD152, is one of the most well-established immune checkpoint molecules expressed predominantly on T cells (Rudd and Schneider, 2003; Yang et al., 2021; Kim and Choi, 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations describing CTLA-4 function.

claim: CTLA-4 primarily regulates the early stages of T-cell activation by attenuating downstream signaling of the T-cell receptor.
source: It primarily regulates the early stages of T-cell activation by attenuating downstream signaling of the T-cell receptor (TCR) (Marengère et al., 1996; Lee et al., 1998; Yokosuka et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on CTLA-4 mechanism of action.

claim: CTLA-4 has a much higher affinity for CD80 and CD86 ligands compared to the co-stimulatory receptor CD28.
source: Specifically, CTLA-4 has a much higher affinity for CD80 and CD86 ligands compared to the co-stimulatory receptor CD28 (Linsley et al., 1994; Collins et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to binding affinity studies.

claim: CTLA-4 provides an inhibitory signal by outcompeting CD28 for ligand binding.
source: By outcompeting CD28 for ligand binding, CTLA-4 provides an inhibitory signal that impacts immunological synapse formation and inhibits T-cell proliferation and activation (Yokosuka et al., 2010; Saito et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to mechanistic studies.

claim: Germline CTLA-4-deficient mice die within 3–4 weeks due to massive T lymphocyte proliferation and the release of inflammatory cytokines.
source: Germline CTLA-4-deficient is lethal for mice within 3–4 wk due to massive T lymphocyte proliferation and the release of inflammatory cytokines (Tivol et al., 1995; Waterhouse et al., 1995; Chambers et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to CTLA-4 knockout mouse studies.

claim: CTLA-4-deficient T lymphocytes exhibit accelerated development of Th2 cells, leading to significantly enhanced secretion of IL-4 and IL-5.
source: Compared to wild-type T lymphocytes, CTLA-4-deficient T lymphocytes exhibit accelerated development of Th2 cells, leading to significantly enhanced secretion of IL-4 and IL-5 (Khattri et al., 1999; Bour-Jordan et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on CTLA-4-deficient T cells.

claim: Conditional deletion of CTLA-4 in adult mice results in rapid immune activation, multiorgan lymphocyte infiltration, and autoantibody production.
source: Additionally, conditional deletion of CTLA-4 in adult mice results in rapid immune activation, multiorgan lymphocyte infiltration, and autoantibody production (Klocke et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a conditional knockout study.

claim: A selective deficiency of CTLA-4 in Treg cells is sufficient to induce lymphoproliferation and autoimmune diseases in mice.
source: Moreover, a selective deficiency of CTLA-4 in Treg cells is sufficient to induce lymphoproliferation and autoimmune diseases in mice (Wing et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a Treg-specific knockout study.

claim: Associations between polymorphic alleles of CTLA-4 and IBD in humans have been reported in multiple studies.
source: Similarly, associations between polymorphic alleles of CTLA-4 and IBD in humans have been reported in multiple studies (Repnik and Potocnik, 2010; Xia et al., 2002; Jiang et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to genetic association studies in humans.

claim: Intestinal inflammation is a common side effect in clinical trials using CTLA-4 as a target for immune checkpoint blockade therapies in cancer treatment.
source: Moreover, CTLA-4 is an intriguing target for novel immune checkpoint blockade therapies in cancer treatment, while intestinal inflammation is a common side effect in these clinical trials (Bamias et al., 2017; Lo et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical trial reports.

claim: Zebrafish is a powerful model system for immunological and biomedical research due to its versatility and high degree of conservation in innate and adaptive immunities.
source: Zebrafish is a powerful model system for immunological and biomedical research, due to its versatility and high degree of conservation in innate and adaptive immunities (Cooper and Alder, 2006; Lam et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to reviews on zebrafish as a model organism.

claim: This study successfully developed an adult vertebrate model with homozygous knockout of the ctla-4 gene for the first time.
source: In our current study, we identified the Ctla-4 homology in zebrafish and successfully developed an adult vertebrate model with homozygous knockout of the ctla-4 gene for the first time.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study describing the generation of the knockout model.

claim: ctla-4-/- zebrafish survive but exhibit attenuated growth and weight loss.
source: These ctla-4-deficient (ctla-4-/-) zebrafish survive but exhibit attenuated growth and weight loss.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations of the ctla-4-/- zebrafish phenotype.

claim: ctla-4 deficiency leads to an IBD-like phenotype in zebrafish characterized by altered intestinal epithelial cell morphology, abnormal inflammatory response, defects in microbial stratification, and composition.
source: Notably, ctla-4 deficiency leads to an IBD-like phenotype in zebrafish characterized by altered intestinal epithelial cell morphology, abnormal inflammatory response, defects in microbial stratification, and composition.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental analyses including histology, transcriptomics, and microbiome analysis.

claim: Ctla-4 exerts its inhibitory function by competing with Cd28 for binding to Cd80/86.
source: Mechanistically, Ctla-4 exerts its inhibitory function by competing with Cd28 for binding to Cd80/86.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data including Co-IP, flow cytometry, and microscale thermophoresis assays.

claim: The ctla-4 knockout zebrafish serves as an innovative platform to elucidate CTLA-4 immunobiology, model human IBD, and develop novel therapeutic modalities.
source: These findings establish the ctla-4 knockout zebrafish as an innovative platform to elucidate CTLA-4 immunobiology, model human IBD, and develop novel therapeutic modalities.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the collective findings of the study.

claim: The zebrafish ctla-4 gene is located on chromosome 9.
source: Through a homology search in the NCBI database, we identified the ctla-4 gene (XM_005167519.4) on zebrafish chromosome 9, which exhibits an exon organization comparable to that of the human CTLA-4 gene (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by database search results and genomic analysis shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Zebrafish Ctla-4 is predicted to be a type I transmembrane protein with a molecular weight of approximately 33 kDa.
source: Zebrafish Ctla-4 is predicted to be a type I transmembrane protein with a molecular weight of approximately 33 kDa, featuring structural characteristics of the immunoglobulin superfamily, which include an N-terminal signal peptide, a single IgV-like extracellular domain, a transmembrane region, and a cytoplasmic tail (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is based on computational prediction and sequence analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Zebrafish Ctla-4 contains a 113LFPPPY118 motif within the ectodomain.
source: Multiple amino acid sequence alignments revealed that Ctla-4 contains a 113LFPPPY118 motif within the ectodomain and a tyrosine-based 206YVKF209 motif in the distal C-terminal region (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Zebrafish Ctla-4 contains a tyrosine-based 206YVKF209 motif in the distal C-terminal region.
source: Multiple amino acid sequence alignments revealed that Ctla-4 contains a 113LFPPPY118 motif within the ectodomain and a tyrosine-based 206YVKF209 motif in the distal C-terminal region (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The LFPPPY and YVKF motifs in zebrafish Ctla-4 closely resemble the MYPPPY and YVKM motifs found in mammalian CTLA-4 homologs.
source: These motifs closely resemble the MYPPPY and YVKM motifs found in mammalian CTLA-4 homologs, which are essential for binding to CD80/CD86 ligands, as well as molecular internalization and signaling inhibition (Marengère et al., 1996; Peach et al., 1994; Shiratori et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is based on sequence comparison and supported by citations to functional studies of mammalian CTLA-4.

claim: Zebrafish Cd28 features a SYPPPF motif in its extracellular region and a FYIQ motif in its intracellular tail.
source: In contrast, zebrafish Cd28 features a SYPPPF motif in its extracellular region and a FYIQ motif in its intracellular tail, distinguishing it from Ctla-4.
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis comparing Cd28 and Ctla-4.

claim: Zebrafish Ctla-4 carries a conserved extracellular 123GNGT126 motif, which is absent in zebrafish Cd28.
source: Additionally, zebrafish Ctla-4, similar to its counterparts in other species, carries a conserved extracellular 123GNGT126 motif, which is absent in zebrafish Cd28 (Bernard et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis and a citation to Bernard et al., 2006.

claim: Phylogenetic analysis showed that zebrafish Ctla-4 clusters with other known CTLA-4 homologs from different species with high bootstrap probability.
source: Consistent with this, phylogenetic analysis showed that Ctla-4 clusters with other known CTLA-4 homologs from different species with high bootstrap probability, whereas zebrafish Cd28 groups separately with other CD28s (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic tree analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Zebrafish Ctla-4 exists as a dimer.
source: Structurally, Ctla-4 exists as a dimer, and unlike the intracellular localization of CTLA-4 in mammals, Ctla-4 is found on the cell membrane (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot analysis under reducing and non-reducing conditions shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Unlike the intracellular localization of CTLA-4 in mammals, zebrafish Ctla-4 is found on the cell membrane.
source: Structurally, Ctla-4 exists as a dimer, and unlike the intracellular localization of CTLA-4 in mammals, Ctla-4 is found on the cell membrane (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by subcellular localization analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ctla-4 is primarily expressed on T cells, including Cd4+ T and Cd8+ T cells.
source: By analyzing the splenic scRNA-seq dataset we recently established (Hu et al., 2023), Ctla-4 was primarily expressed on the T cells, including the Cd4+ T and Cd8+ T cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Immunofluorescence assays on splenic leukocytes verified that Ctla-4 is expressed on T cells.
source: This result was verified by immunofluorescence assays on the splenic leukocytes (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 1F.

claim: A 14-base deletion in the second exon of the ctla-4 gene was generated using CRISPR/Cas9.
source: To further investigate the function of Ctla-4, we generated a ctla-4-/- zebrafish line with a 14-base deletion in the second exon of the ctla-4 gene (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by genotyping and sequencing data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: The body weight of ctla-4-/- zebrafish was significantly reduced compared with wild-type zebrafish.
source: The zebrafish appeared grossly normal in appearance; however, the body weight and size were significantly reduced compared with those of wild-type zebrafish (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The size of ctla-4-/- zebrafish was significantly reduced compared with wild-type zebrafish.
source: The zebrafish appeared grossly normal in appearance; however, the body weight and size were significantly reduced compared with those of wild-type zebrafish (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by visual observation and measurements shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: ctla-4-/- zebrafish were featured by intestine shortening.
source: Anatomically, the ctla-4-/- zebrafish were featured by intestine shortening and splenomegaly, suggesting the occurrence of chronic inflammation in the intestines (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical measurements shown in Figure 2F.

claim: ctla-4-/- zebrafish were featured by splenomegaly.
source: Anatomically, the ctla-4-/- zebrafish were featured by intestine shortening and splenomegaly, suggesting the occurrence of chronic inflammation in the intestines (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical measurements shown in Figure 2G.

claim: ctla-4-/- zebrafish exhibited significant epithelial hyperplasia in the anterior intestine segment.
source: Compared to the wild-type zebrafish, the ctla-4-/- fish exhibited significant epithelial hyperplasia in the anterior intestine segment, accompanied with a small amount of mucosal inflammatory cell infiltration (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by H&E staining analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: ctla-4-/- zebrafish exhibited mucosal inflammatory cell infiltration in the anterior intestine.
source: Compared to the wild-type zebrafish, the ctla-4-/- fish exhibited significant epithelial hyperplasia in the anterior intestine segment, accompanied with a small amount of mucosal inflammatory cell infiltration (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by H&E staining analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Noteworthy goblet cell loss was observed in ctla-4-/- anterior intestine.
source: Moreover, noteworthy goblet cell loss, reduction of normal mucins, and the accumulation of acidic mucins were also observed in ctla-4-/- anterior intestine, as detected through Alcian Blue and Periodic Acid-Schiff (AB-PAS) or PAS staining (Figure 2I and J, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by AB-PAS and PAS staining shown in Figure 2I and J.

claim: Reduction of normal mucins was observed in ctla-4-/- anterior intestine.
source: Moreover, noteworthy goblet cell loss, reduction of normal mucins, and the accumulation of acidic mucins were also observed in ctla-4-/- anterior intestine, as detected through Alcian Blue and Periodic Acid-Schiff (AB-PAS) or PAS staining (Figure 2I and J, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by AB-PAS and PAS staining shown in Figure 2I and J.

claim: The accumulation of acidic mucins was observed in ctla-4-/- anterior intestine.
source: Moreover, noteworthy goblet cell loss, reduction of normal mucins, and the accumulation of acidic mucins were also observed in ctla-4-/- anterior intestine, as detected through Alcian Blue and Periodic Acid-Schiff (AB-PAS) or PAS staining (Figure 2I and J, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by AB-PAS and PAS staining shown in Figure 2I and J.

claim: A small amount of lymphocytic infiltration occurred in the mid-intestine segment of ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: A small amount of lymphocytic infiltration and mild epithelial damage occurred in the mid-intestine segment of ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by H&E staining analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Mild epithelial damage occurred in the mid-intestine segment of ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: A small amount of lymphocytic infiltration and mild epithelial damage occurred in the mid-intestine segment of ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by H&E staining analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: In the posterior intestine of ctla-4-/- fish, the intestinal villi were markedly shortened.
source: In the posterior intestine of ctla-4-/- fish, the intestinal villi were markedly shortened, the epithelial barrier showed severely disrupted, and the intestinal wall became thinner, wherein the mucosal and transmural inflammatory cells were significantly infiltrated (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by H&E staining analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The epithelial barrier in the posterior intestine of ctla-4-/- fish showed severe disruption.
source: In the posterior intestine of ctla-4-/- fish, the intestinal villi were markedly shortened, the epithelial barrier showed severely disrupted, and the intestinal wall became thinner, wherein the mucosal and transmural inflammatory cells were significantly infiltrated (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by H&E staining analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The intestinal wall in the posterior intestine of ctla-4-/- fish became thinner.
source: In the posterior intestine of ctla-4-/- fish, the intestinal villi were markedly shortened, the epithelial barrier showed severely disrupted, and the intestinal wall became thinner, wherein the mucosal and transmural inflammatory cells were significantly infiltrated (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by H&E staining analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Mucosal and transmural inflammatory cells were significantly infiltrated in the posterior intestine of ctla-4-/- fish.
source: In the posterior intestine of ctla-4-/- fish, the intestinal villi were markedly shortened, the epithelial barrier showed severely disrupted, and the intestinal wall became thinner, wherein the mucosal and transmural inflammatory cells were significantly infiltrated (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by H&E staining analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The intestinal lumens in all three intestinal segments were enlarged in the ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: Notably, the intestinal lumens in all three intestinal segments were enlarged in the ctla-4-/- zebrafish, and the ratio between the length of the intestinal villi and the intestinal ring radius was higher in the ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines compared to those in wild-type zebrafish (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The ratio between the length of the intestinal villi and the intestinal ring radius was higher in the ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines compared to wild-type zebrafish.
source: Notably, the intestinal lumens in all three intestinal segments were enlarged in the ctla-4-/- zebrafish, and the ratio between the length of the intestinal villi and the intestinal ring radius was higher in the ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines compared to those in wild-type zebrafish (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The epithelial cells of posterior intestine in ctla-4-/- zebrafish exhibited alteration in tight junction.
source: In addition, the ultrastructure analysis revealed that the epithelial cells of posterior intestine in ctla-4-/- zebrafish exhibited alteration in tight junction, the loss of adhesion junctions and desmosomes, and disruption of microvilli (Figure 2K).
evidence: This claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy analysis shown in Figure 2K.

claim: The epithelial cells of posterior intestine in ctla-4-/- zebrafish exhibited loss of adhesion junctions and desmosomes.
source: In addition, the ultrastructure analysis revealed that the epithelial cells of posterior intestine in ctla-4-/- zebrafish exhibited alteration in tight junction, the loss of adhesion junctions and desmosomes, and disruption of microvilli (Figure 2K).
evidence: This claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy analysis shown in Figure 2K.

claim: The epithelial cells of posterior intestine in ctla-4-/- zebrafish exhibited disruption of microvilli.
source: In addition, the ultrastructure analysis revealed that the epithelial cells of posterior intestine in ctla-4-/- zebrafish exhibited alteration in tight junction, the loss of adhesion junctions and desmosomes, and disruption of microvilli (Figure 2K).
evidence: This claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy analysis shown in Figure 2K.

claim: A total of 1140 differentially expressed genes were identified in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines, with 714 genes up-regulated and 426 genes down-regulated.
source: We identified a total of 1140 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), among which 714 genes were up-regulated, and 426 genes were down-regulated in ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: GO enrichment analysis showed that DEGs in the top 10 enriched biological processes were associated with immune response and inflammatory response.
source: GO enrichment analysis showed that DEGs or up-regulated genes in the top 10 enriched biological processes were associated with the immune response and inflammatory response (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The up-regulated DEGs are primarily involved in cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction and cell adhesion molecules.
source: Moreover, the KEGG enrichment analyses indicated that the up-regulated DEGs are primarily involved in the process of cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction and cell adhesion molecules, which are also related to inflammation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This claim is supported by KEGG enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The down-regulated DEGs were significantly enriched in metabolic processes.
source: however, the down-regulated DEGs were significantly enriched in the process of metabolism (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by KEGG enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The intestines of ctla-4-/- zebrafish showed significant upregulation of il1b, tnfa, mpx, mmp9, cxcl8a, and il13.
source: The intestines of ctla-4-/- zebrafish showed significant upregulation of il1b, tnfa, myeloid-specific peroxidase (mpx), matrix metallopeptidase 9 (mmp9), chemokine (C-X-C motif) ligand 8 a (cxcl8a), and il13.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and confirmed by RT-qPCR.

claim: il10 was markedly down-regulated in Ctla-4-deficient intestines.
source: In contrast, il10, a potent anti-inflammatory cytokine, was markedly down-regulated in Ctla-4-deficient intestines (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: il1b was a major cytokine that played a hub role in promoting the bowel inflammation of ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: By constructing the protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, we found that il1b was a major cytokine that played a hub role in promoting the bowel inflammation of ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is based on PPI network analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Genes involved in lymphocyte chemotaxis were positively enriched in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines.
source: Moreover, Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) showed that genes involved in the lymphocyte chemotaxis, positive regulation of ERK1 and ERK2 cascade, Calcium and MAPK signaling pathways were positively enriched in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines, implying a sensitized or activated state of lymphocytes due to the absence of Ctla-4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Genes involved in positive regulation of ERK1 and ERK2 cascade were positively enriched in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines.
source: Moreover, Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) showed that genes involved in the lymphocyte chemotaxis, positive regulation of ERK1 and ERK2 cascade, Calcium and MAPK signaling pathways were positively enriched in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines, implying a sensitized or activated state of lymphocytes due to the absence of Ctla-4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Genes involved in Calcium and MAPK signaling pathways were positively enriched in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines.
source: Moreover, Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) showed that genes involved in the lymphocyte chemotaxis, positive regulation of ERK1 and ERK2 cascade, Calcium and MAPK signaling pathways were positively enriched in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines, implying a sensitized or activated state of lymphocytes due to the absence of Ctla-4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Biological processes related to neutrophil activation and chemotaxis were significantly enriched in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines.
source: Notably, biological processes related to neutrophil activation and chemotaxis were significantly enriched (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: MPO activity was markedly increased in the intestines and peripheral blood of ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: As a support, MPO activity was markedly increased in the intestines and peripheral blood of ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 3H).
evidence: This claim is supported by MPO activity assay shown in Figure 3H.

claim: A number of IBD biomarkers observed in mammals were highly expressed in the ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: Besides, a number of biological markers or susceptibility genes of IBD observed in mammals, including c-reactive protein 6 (crp6), crp7, MMPs, haptoglobin, il23r, insulin-like growth factor binding protein 1 a (igfbp1a), cAMP responsive element modulator b (cremb), and lymphocyte specific protein 1 b (lsp1b), were highly expressed in the ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 3I and J; Duerr et al., 2006; Lees et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2017)
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3I and J, with citations to mammalian IBD studies.

claim: Nine discrete cell clusters were obtained from 7,539 cells of wild-type and ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines by scRNA-seq analysis.
source: We obtained nine discrete clusters from 7,539 cells of wild-type and ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The cell clusters were classified as enterocytes, enteroendocrine cells, smooth muscle cells, neutrophils, macrophages, B cells, and T/NK/ILC-like cells.
source: These clusters of cells were classified as enterocytes, enteroendocrine cells, smooth muscle cells, neutrophils, macrophages, B cells, and a group of T/NK/ILC-like cells based on their co-expression of lineage marker genes (Figure 4B and C, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by marker gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: The apoptotic pathway was highly enriched in enterocytes of ctla4-/- zebrafish.
source: KEGG analysis showed that apoptotic pathway was highly enriched in enterocytes of ctla4-/- zebrafish, suggesting that aberrant apoptosis contributes to the epithelial injury (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by KEGG analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: A higher number of apoptotic cells were detected in the intestines of ctla4-/- zebrafish by TUNEL assay.
source: Subsequently, we conducted a TUNEL assay to detect apoptosis in the posterior intestines from both wild-type and ctla4-/- zebrafish. The results showed a higher number of apoptotic cells in the intestines of ctla4-/- zebrafish (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by TUNEL assay results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Genes involved in the formation of tight and adhesion junctions were significantly down-regulated in enterocytes of ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: Additionally, genes functionally involved in the formation of tight and adhesion junctions, such as oclna, cdh1, pcdh1b, and cldn15a, were significantly down-regulated in enterocytes of ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 4D)
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Inflammation-related genes and pathways were significantly up-regulated and enriched in neutrophils, B cells, and macrophages of ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: Furthermore, inflammation-related genes and pathways were significantly up-regulated and enriched in neutrophils, B cells, and macrophages of ctla-4-/- zebrafish, suggesting active inflammatory responses (Figure 4E–G, Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 4E-G.

claim: Six subpopulations were classified from T/NK/ILC-like cell groups including Cd8+ T cells, ILC3-like cells, maturing Ccr7high T cells, NKT-like cells, and two groups of Th2 cells.
source: By sub-clustering analysis, six subpopulations were classified from T/NK/ILC-like cell groups based on their expression with a set of marker genes. These subpopulations include Cd8+ T cells, ILC3-like cells, maturing Ccr7high T cells, NKT-like cells, and two groups of Th2 cells (Figure 5A–C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by sub-clustering analysis shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: The abundances of NKT-like and two subsets of Th2 cells were significantly increased in the intestines of ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: The abundances of NKT-like and two subsets of Th2 cells were significantly increased in the intestines of ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 5D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell abundance analysis shown in Figure 5D-F.

claim: NKT-like and Th2 cells exhibited high expression levels of il13.
source: These cells exhibited high expression levels of il13 (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5G and H.

claim: The second subset of Th2 cells was seldom observed in the intestine of wild-type zebrafish.
source: Specifically, the second subset of Th2 cells was seldom observed in the intestine of wild-type zebrafish, indicating their unique role in the pathogenesis of IBD-like phenotype in ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 5D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell abundance analysis shown in Figure 5D-F.

claim: Ctla-4 deficiency is positively associated with inflammatory cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, PPAR, calcium, and MAPK signaling pathways in NKT-like and Th2 cells.
source: KEGG analysis of up-regulated genes from ctla-4-/- NKT-like and Th2 cells indicated that Ctla-4 deficiency is positively associated with the inflammatory cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, PPAR, calcium, and MAPK signaling pathways, cellular adhesion, and mucosal immune responses (Figure 5I and J, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by KEGG analysis shown in Figure 5I and J.

claim: The proportion of ILC3-like cells was decreased in Ctla-4-deficient intestines.
source: Notably, the proportion of ILC3-like cells was decreased, and they highly expressed il17a/f1 and il17a/f3 in the Ctla-4-deficient intestines (Figure 5D–F and K).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell abundance analysis shown in Figure 5D-F.

claim: ILC3-like cells highly expressed il17a/f1 and il17a/f3 in the Ctla-4-deficient intestines.
source: Notably, the proportion of ILC3-like cells was decreased, and they highly expressed il17a/f1 and il17a/f3 in the Ctla-4-deficient intestines (Figure 5D–F and K).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5K.

claim: A substantial decline in the population of ILC3s has been consistently reported within inflamed intestines.
source: Investigations have consistently reported a substantial decline in the population of ILC3s within the inflamed intestines and IL-17A-secreting ILC3s play a significant role in the development of intestinal inflammation (Bernink et al., 2013; Li et al., 2017; Martin et al., 2019; Buonocore et al., 2010; Ermann et al., 2014; Aparicio-Domingo et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies on ILC3s in intestinal inflammation.

claim: IL-17A-secreting ILC3s play a significant role in the development of intestinal inflammation.
source: Investigations have consistently reported a substantial decline in the population of ILC3s within the inflamed intestines and IL-17A-secreting ILC3s play a significant role in the development of intestinal inflammation (Bernink et al., 2013; Li et al., 2017; Martin et al., 2019; Buonocore et al., 2010; Ermann et al., 2014; Aparicio-Domingo et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies on ILC3s in intestinal inflammation.

claim: Wild-type zebrafish intestines had a significantly higher number of amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) compared to ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: The results revealed a significantly higher number of amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) in wild-type zebrafish intestines, with 730 ASVs unique to the wild-type group and 276 ASVs exclusively found in ctla-4-/- group (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by 16S rRNA gene sequencing analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The Shannon index and Simpson index indicated a decreased microbial diversity in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines.
source: Furthermore, the Shannon index and the Simpson index indicated a decreased microbial diversity in ctla-4-/- zebrafish intestines (Figure 6B)
evidence: This claim is supported by alpha diversity analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Principal Coordinate Analysis using Bray-Curtis distance revealed a significant separation in the microbial composition between ctla-4-/- group and the wild-type group.
source: and the Principal Coordinate Analysis (PCoA) using Bray-Curtis distance revealed a significant separation in the microbial composition between ctla-4-/- group and the wild-type group (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by beta diversity analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Alphaproteobacteria and Gammaproteobacteria were found to be the most prevalent classes in zebrafish intestinal microbiota.
source: Alphaproteobacteria and Gammaproteobacteria were found to be the most prevalent classes.
evidence: This claim is based on taxonomic analysis of the microbiome data.

claim: Ctla-4 deficiency resulted in a significant reduction in Alphaproteobacteria abundance.
source: Relative to wild-type group, Ctla-4 deficiency resulted in a significant reduction in Alphaproteobacteria abundance.
evidence: This claim is supported by microbiome composition analysis.

claim: Gammaproteobacteria abundance increased in ctla-4-/- zebrafish, although the change did not reach statistical significance.
source: However, the Gammaproteobacteria, one of the main classes of Gamma-negative pathogenic bacteria expanded under inflammation conditions, was increased, although the change did not reach statistical significance (Figure 6D and E; Zhao et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by microbiome composition analysis shown in Figure 6D and E, with a citation.

claim: A decreased relative abundance of SCFAs-producing Bacilli was observed in ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: In addition, we observed a decreased relative abundance of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs)-producing Bacilli and Verrucomicrobiae, the latter of which contributes to glucose homeostasis and intestinal health (Figure 6F and G; Xu et al., 2020; Belzer and de Vos, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by microbiome composition analysis shown in Figure 6F and G.

claim: A decreased relative abundance of Verrucomicrobiae was observed in ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: In addition, we observed a decreased relative abundance of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs)-producing Bacilli and Verrucomicrobiae, the latter of which contributes to glucose homeostasis and intestinal health (Figure 6F and G; Xu et al., 2020; Belzer and de Vos, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by microbiome composition analysis shown in Figure 6F and G.

claim: A notable enrichment of Enterobacteriaceae was observed in ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: Notably, the family-level analysis revealed a notable enrichment of Enterobacteriaceae, overgrowing under host inflammatory conditions, and the Shewanellaceae, serving as the most important secondary or opportunistic pathogens, in ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 6H and I).
evidence: This claim is supported by family-level microbiome analysis shown in Figure 6H and I.

claim: A notable enrichment of Shewanellaceae was observed in ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: Notably, the family-level analysis revealed a notable enrichment of Enterobacteriaceae, overgrowing under host inflammatory conditions, and the Shewanellaceae, serving as the most important secondary or opportunistic pathogens, in ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 6H and I).
evidence: This claim is supported by family-level microbiome analysis shown in Figure 6H and I.

claim: Several potentially opportunistic pathogens, including Gammaproteobacteria, Enterobacterales, and Aeromonadales were found to be overrepresented in ctla-4-/- zebrafish by LEfSe analysis.
source: The results showed that several potentially opportunistic pathogens, including Gammaproteobacteria, Enterobacterales, and Aeromonadales were found to be overrepresented in ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 6J).
evidence: This claim is supported by LEfSe analysis shown in Figure 6J.

claim: Actinobacteriota, Cetobacterium, and Planctomycetota were more abundant in the wild-type zebrafish compared to ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: In contrast, Actinobacteriota, Cetobacterium, and Planctomycetota (Planctomycetes) were more abundant in the wild-type zebrafish.
evidence: This claim is supported by LEfSe analysis of differential bacterial taxa.

claim: The proliferation of lymphocytes from ctla-4-/- zebrafish was more pronounced compared to wild-type controls.
source: As expected, the proliferation of lymphocytes from ctla-4-/- zebrafish was more pronounced compared to wild-type controls, and the addition of sCtla-4-Ig effectively suppressed this proliferation (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mixed lymphocyte reaction assays shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: The addition of sCtla-4-Ig effectively suppressed the proliferation of lymphocytes from ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: As expected, the proliferation of lymphocytes from ctla-4-/- zebrafish was more pronounced compared to wild-type controls, and the addition of sCtla-4-Ig effectively suppressed this proliferation (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mixed lymphocyte reaction assays shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Blockade of Ctla-4 using anti-Ctla-4 Ab significantly promoted the proliferation of lymphocytes from wild-type zebrafish.
source: Consistent with these results, blockade of Ctla-4 using anti-Ctla-4 Ab significantly promoted the proliferation of lymphocytes from wild-type zebrafish (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by antibody blockade assays shown in Figure 7C.

claim: sCd28-Ig administration inhibited the proliferation of lymphocytes from ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: Furthermore, sCd28-Ig administration inhibited the proliferation of lymphocytes from ctla-4-/- zebrafish (Figure 7D)
evidence: This claim is supported by soluble protein administration assays shown in Figure 7D.

claim: sCd80/86 promoted the expansion of Ctla-4-deficient lymphocytes.
source: whereas sCd80/86 promoted the expansion of Ctla-4-deficient lymphocytes (Figure 7E).
evidence: This claim is supported by soluble protein administration assays shown in Figure 7E.

claim: AlphaFold2 predictions indicated that both Cd28 and Ctla-4 form a well-defined interface with Cd80/86, utilizing the same binding site.
source: The predictions indicated that both Cd28 and Ctla-4 form a well-defined interface with Cd80/86, utilizing the same binding site (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This claim is based on computational structure prediction shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: Co-immunoprecipitation assays provided evidence for the molecular interactions between Cd80/86 and Cd28 or Ctla-4.
source: Subsequently, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assays were conducted to provide compelling evidence for the molecular interactions between Cd80/86 and Cd28 or Ctla-4.
evidence: This claim is supported by Co-IP experimental data.

claim: Flow cytometry analysis revealed dose-dependent associations between Cd80/86 and Cd28 or Ctla-4 in HEK293T cells.
source: Flow cytometry analysis further revealed dose-dependent associations between Cd80/86 and Cd28 or Ctla-4 in HEK293T cells (Figure 7H, Figure 7—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7H and Figure 7—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Ctla-4 exhibits a higher binding affinity for Cd80/86 than Cd28, as evidenced by a lower equilibrium association constant value (KD = 0.50 ± 0.25 μM vs. KD = 2.64 ± 0.45 μM).
source: Additionally, microscale thermophoresis assays demonstrated that Ctla-4 exhibits a higher binding affinity for Cd80/86 than Cd28, as evidenced by a lower equilibrium association constant value (KD = 0.50 ± 0.25 μM vs. KD = 2.64 ± 0.45 μM) (Figure 7I).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscale thermophoresis assay data shown in Figure 7I.

claim: Ctla-4-deficient zebrafish treated with sCtla-4-Ig exhibited obvious body weight restoration compared to those treated with the IgG isotype control.
source: This is supported by the observation that Ctla-4-deficient zebrafish treated with sCtla-4-Ig exhibited obvious body weight restoration compared to those treated with the IgG isotype control (Figure 8A).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo treatment data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Ctla-4-Ig treatment resulted in a significant decrease in lymphocyte infiltration in the posterior intestine of ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: As expected, Ctla-4-Ig treatment resulted in a significant decrease in lymphocyte infiltration and an improvement in the epithelial barrier (Figure 8B).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Ctla-4-Ig treatment resulted in an improvement in the epithelial barrier in the posterior intestine of ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: As expected, Ctla-4-Ig treatment resulted in a significant decrease in lymphocyte infiltration and an improvement in the epithelial barrier (Figure 8B).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Ctla-4-Ig treatment significantly reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory genes including il13, tnfa, mpx, mmp9, and cxcl8a in ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: Moreover, Ctla-4-Ig treatment significantly reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory genes, including il13, tnfa, mpx, mmp9, and cxcl8a, as well as igfbp1a, cremb, and lsp1a, which are susceptibility genes for IBD observed in mammals (Figure 8C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 8C and D.

claim: Ctla-4-Ig treatment significantly reduced the expression of IBD susceptibility genes including igfbp1a, cremb, and lsp1a in ctla-4-/- zebrafish.
source: Moreover, Ctla-4-Ig treatment significantly reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory genes, including il13, tnfa, mpx, mmp9, and cxcl8a, as well as igfbp1a, cremb, and lsp1a, which are susceptibility genes for IBD observed in mammals (Figure 8C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 8C and D.

claim: Lower microbiota diversity has consistently been observed in patients with IBD phenotype.
source: Notably, lower microbiota diversity has consistently been observed in patients with IBD phenotype (Ott et al., 2004; Manichanh et al., 2006), making it a valuable indicator of host health.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on microbiota diversity in IBD patients.

claim: Neutrophils can induce histopathological effects through releasing matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), neutrophil elastase, and myeloperoxidase (MPO).
source: Studies have shown that neutrophils can induce histopathological effects through releasing matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), neutrophil elastase, and myeloperoxidase (MPO) (Butin-Israeli et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a study on neutrophil function.

claim: IL-1β and TNF-α act as crucial mediators in mammalian IBD models by disrupting epithelial junctions and inducing apoptosis of epithelial cells.
source: This is consistent with studies showing that IL-1β and TNF-α act as crucial mediators in mammalian IBD models by disrupting epithelial junctions and inducing apoptosis of epithelial cells (Al-Sadi et al., 2013a; Al-Sadi et al., 2013b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on cytokine function in IBD.

claim: IL-13 directly contributes to epithelial cell damage by disrupting tight junctions, inducing apoptosis, and impairing cellular restitution.
source: Furthermore, IL-13, a key effector Th2 cytokine, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of ulcerative colitis in mammals, where it directly contributes to epithelial cell damage by disrupting tight junctions, inducing apoptosis, and impairing cellular restitution (Heller et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a study on IL-13 function in ulcerative colitis.

claim: ILC3 plays a protective role in IBD in mammals by promoting epithelial cell proliferation and survival, as well as enhancing intestinal barrier function through the production of IL-22.
source: ILC3 is the most abundant type of ILCs in the intestines and plays a protective role in IBD in mammals by promoting epithelial cell proliferation and survival, as well as enhancing intestinal barrier function through the production of IL-22 (Buonocore et al., 2010; Aparicio-Domingo et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on ILC3 function in IBD.

claim: The common feature of microbiota changes in IBD is the expansion of Proteobacteria, particularly members of the Enterobacteriaceae family.
source: The common feature of these changes is the expansion of Proteobacteria, particularly members of the Enterobacteriaceae family (Shin et al., 2015; Winter et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on microbiota changes in IBD.

claim: Reduced microbial diversity in IBD results from the loss of normal anaerobic bacteria, such as Bacteroides, Eubacterium, and Lactobacillus.
source: Previous studies suggest that reduced microbial diversity in IBD results from the loss of normal anaerobic bacteria, such as Bacteroides, Eubacterium, and Lactobacillus (Ott et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a study on microbial diversity in IBD.

claim: Inflammation-driven increases in intestinal lumen oxygenation and the availability of nitrate and host-derived electron acceptors facilitate anaerobic respiration and Enterobacteriaceae proliferation.
source: Concurrently, inflammation-driven increases in intestinal lumen oxygenation and the availability of nitrate and host-derived electron acceptors facilitate anaerobic respiration and Enterobacteriaceae proliferation (Hughes et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a study on the relationship between inflammation and microbiota changes.

claim: Gut microbiota exposure induces local IL-23 production, which upregulates CTLA-4 on ILC3s.
source: Recently, gut microbiota exposure has been found to induce local IL-23 production, which upregulates CTLA-4 on ILC3s. This supports immune regulation by reducing CD80/86 co-stimulatory signaling and increasing PD-L1 bioavailability on myeloid cells. Impairment of this pathway manifests in a substantial imbalance of effector and regulatory T cell responses, exacerbating intestinal inflammation (Ahmed et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ahmed et al., 2024.
